title: hoa_paint_color_revenge
beats: I got a $50 fine for my mailbox post being "the wrong shade of white."
My HOA president (61F) said I had exactly 14 days to repaint it or face daily fines.
Small detail: three months earlier, she'd begged me to design her granddaughter's birthday invitations because I do graphic design.
I never sent her an invoice for that. I just said "don't worry about it."
So I complied. I repainted the post the exact approved shade of white, on day 13, like a good citizen.
Then I mailed her an invoice for the birthday invitations. $50. Due in 14 days.
She called me, furious, saying that was a favor between neighbors.
I said, "Funny, that's exactly what I thought my mailbox post was."
She threatened to take it to the HOA board.
I told her to go ahead, and mentioned I'd also be attending, with my original fine notice and her texts begging for "just a cute little invite, no rush."
The board voted to waive my fine unanimously.
They also suggested she stop assigning fines for shades of white you need a paint chip and a law degree to identify.
In cash. In an envelope. Slid under my door like contraband.
